summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, COPD, insulin-dependent diabetes, and polysubstance use was admitted after a syncopal episode following alcohol consumption and recent cocaine use. He presented with loss of consciousness upon standing, without prodromal symptoms, chest pain, or shortness of breath. Initial evaluation revealed stable vital signs, no evidence of intracranial injury on CT, and no arrhythmias or acute ischemia. Labs showed elevated BNP and mild troponin elevation without dynamic changes, along with iron deficiency anemia. A gout flare in the right great toe was treated with colchicine. He remained hemodynamically stable, with improvement in symptoms and no recurrent syncope. Discharge was planned with once-daily torsemide, continued management of chronic conditions, and emphasis on substance use cessation. Follow-up was arranged with primary care and cardiology, particularly regarding defibrillator eligibility.
problems: Poisoning by cocaine, accidental (unintentional), initial encounter
Cardiomyopathy due to drug and external agent
Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
